title: ctdl-validate report
description: The shape of `ctdl-validate --format json`. Every report carries `report_schema_version`, which is the version of this document and not the version of the tool. `additionalProperties` is false everywhere on purpose: a consumer that validates against this schema learns about a new key rather than ignoring it.

report_schema_version.description: The version of this schema that the report conforms to. Semantic: the major part changes when a consumer that reads the old shape would break.

version.description: The tool's own version, which moves independently of report_schema_version.

document.description: How much of the document the run had jurisdiction over. `entities` is every entity the walk registered, nested ones included; `checked_entities` is how many of those declare at least one ceterms: or ceasn: term, as a @type or as a property key. An empty `findings` array means the payload tripped no rule, and that is not the same fact as the payload having been checked: a document declaring none of those terms trips nothing because there is nothing in it this tool reads. Measured 2026-09-07: package.json, tsconfig.json, {}, [] and this repository's own vendored context.json each produced a report indistinguishable from a clean CTDL payload's. A `checked_entities` of zero tells them apart.

findings.description: Every finding, deduplicated and in the tool's own deterministic order. An empty array means the payload tripped no rule, which is not the same as a payload that was fully checked; UNVERIFIABLE findings are how the difference is reported, and `document.checked_entities` says whether anything was in scope at all.

summary.description: How many findings of each severity. Every severity is always present, including the ones that are zero: a consumer must never have to read the absence of a key as a count of none.

measured_count.description: A count, or null when the producer did not measure it. Three states, not two: null is not zero, and a consumer must not read it as one. The CLI and the playground always measure; a caller rendering findings it assembled by hand has no document to measure, and a count invented for it would be exactly the defect this field exists to remove.

severity.description: ERROR gates the exit code. UNVERIFIABLE never does; it marks what the payload alone cannot settle, and it is never a pass.

rule.description: The published rule a finding is made under, with the source it was read from and the date it was read. Never a rule written from memory.

url.description: Where the rule was read. A URL for a published rule; for this tool's own stated policy, the document and section that states it.

retrieved.description: The date the cited source was downloaded, ISO 8601, or "-" when the citation is tool policy rather than an external document.

suggestion.description: A re-spelling this run determined from its own input: a value already written in the document, or in a document supplied with --resolve, that the finding's defect calls for. Present only under --suggest, offered only where exactly one candidate exists, and never a claim about what was meant.

difference.description: What a reader would have to change, in the tool's own vocabulary.

code.description: The stable identifier of what was found.

entity.description: The @id of the entity the finding is about, or the tool's own name for an entity that declares none.

property.description: The CTDL property, or the tool's name for the aspect, the finding is about.

value.description: The value as written, rendered as a string. "(absent)" where the finding is that nothing was written.

suggestions.description: Determined re-spellings for this finding. Absent unless --suggest is on and this run derived at least one; absent is not the same as an empty array, and no report writes one. A code the tool refuses to suggest for -- a bare UUID, a missing language tag, anything UNVERIFIABLE -- never carries this key, and src/ctdl_validate/suggest.py says why for each.
